# Draft:The Palladium Global Science Award

----
}}
The Palladium Global Science Award (PGSA) is an international competition launched in 2025 to support scientific and applied projects exploring new uses of palladium. The first edition attracted nearly 100 entries from over 30 countries, and its inaugural ceremony took place on November 21, 2025, in Hong Kong, where five scientists from Canada, Japan, India, the United States, and Saudi Arabia shared a prize fund of US$350,000.
Organization and partners
The competition is organized by the China Precious Metals Industry Committee (CPMIC), with partners Shanghai Metals Market, North-West University (South Africa), and the MDX Research Center for Element Strategy at the Institute of Science Tokyo.
Nominations and prize fund
The competition includes three categories of new palladium applications—Best Scientific Development (US$120,000 for first place and US$60,000 for second), Best Scientific Article (US$80,000 and US$40,000), and Best Applied Concept (US$50,000 for first place)—with a total prize fund of US$350,000.
Jury
Applications are evaluated by an international jury of leading scientists and experts from major universities and research centers worldwide:
* Jury chairman Prof. Francis Verpoort — Chair Professor, State Key Laboratory of Advanced Technology for Material Synthesis and Processing, Wuhan University of Technology, China; Professor, Joint Institute of Chemical Research (FFMiEN).
* Prof. Kyriaki Polychronopoulou — Full Professor of Mechanical and Nuclear Engineering; Acting Chair and Director, Center for Catalysis and Separations (CeCaS), Khalifa University of Science and Technology, UAE.
* Prof. Dmitri Bessarabov — Professor, North-West University, South Africa; Director, HySA Infrastructure Center of Competence.
* Prof. Chao Chen — Associate Professor and Principal Investigator, Department of Chemistry, Tsinghua University, China.
* Prof. Dr. Lutz Ackermann — Full Professor, Institute for Organic and Biomolecular Chemistry; Director, Wöhler Research Institute for Sustainable Chemistry, Georg-August-Universität Göttingen, Germany; Associate Editor, Chemical Communications.
Laureates
Best Scientific Development
* First Prize: Professor Chao-Jun Li (McGill University, Canada) — for the development of a palladium-doped semiconductor capable of simultaneously activating methane (CH₄) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) under light irradiation to produce green methanol. The technology enables the conversion of harmful emissions into valuable chemical products.
* Second Prize: Professor Makoto Fujita (University of Tokyo and Institute for Molecular Science, Japan) — for the development of a self-assembly method for large palladium nanocages, leading to the "crystalline sponge" technique for determining molecular structures.
Best Scientific Article
* First Prize: Professor Natesan Thirupathi (University of Delhi, India) — for a scientific article on cyclopalladation of organopalladium compounds, contributing to more efficient and environmentally friendly pharmaceutical synthesis.
* Second Prize: Professor Michael J. Krische (University of Texas at Austin, United States) — for research on new hydrogen-transfer-mediated cross-coupling methods using sodium formate, offering safer and more cost-effective routes for synthesizing medically important compounds.
Best Applied Concept
* First Prize: Dr Safa Faris Kayed (Prince Sattam bin Abdulaziz University, Saudi Arabia) — for the PalladClear project, a palladium-based photocatalytic device designed to remove hazardous dyes and pharmaceutical residues from industrial wastewater. The system enables on-site degradation of persistent pollutants into harmless substances.
